utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: We were able to see on that programme how Spegelj was telling his associates that groups of five men must be formed to go to army officers' houses door-to-door, kill them at their doorsteps so that at the key critical moment not a single officer would be able to reach his barracks.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did Spegelj say then that it would be civil war without mercy? There would be no mercy even for women or children. Simply they would throw bombs into the family homes of Yugoslav officers.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you remember that Martin Spegelj as Tudjman's minister of defence said that the problem of Knin and the Serbs in Knin would be dealt with by massacre?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did Tudjman establish quite illegally a paramilitary formation called the Home Guards Corps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was illegal under the Federal laws then.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Under the constitutional and legal system of Yugoslavia it was completely illegal, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: At the largest stadium in Zagreb did he organise a parade and inspection of the Home Guards Corps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: In the eyes of the Serbian people, did that mean officialising an Ustasha army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It certainly caused terror among the Serbs because a new army was created they were not represented in.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did the Croatian Democratic Union as Tudjman's ruling party begin to arm its members?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You said on one occasion that on your way from Osijek via Slovanska Pozega to Pakrac, in many places in Slavonia you saw armed civilians carrying rifles in Croatian places. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did Franjo Tudjman increase the force, the numbers of Croatian police many times?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did that police force now accept almost exclusively members of his party?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did an openly Ustasha political party, the Croatian Party of Rights, form its own paramilitary formation called Croatian Armed Forces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That political party made their own army that was called this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did they display openly all Ustasha symbols?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did Tudjman's government start making demands that the Yugoslav People's Army leave Croatia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did they begin blocking barracks, cutting off power, water, telephone lines to the barracks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did they start killing soldiers, attacking them, injuring them, killing them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: In Split was a JNA soldier killed, a Macedonian called Sasko Gesovski?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Was the garrison in Varazdin blockaded in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Was an entire corps under siege there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did that corps have 120 tanks which were the most up-to-date tanks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: At the end did the corps commander finally surrender and deliver all those weapons to the Croats?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Were some officers killed in spite of having surrendered?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: In the barracks in Bjelovar did Major Tepic refuse to surrender and did he blow-up both himself and a group of soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Because he didn't want to surrender to Tudjman's paramilitary forces; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did Croatian propaganda persistently call the JNA a Jugo-Communist army, then a Jugo-Chetnik army, and then finally a Serbo-Chetnik army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: When the armed operations began did Croatian propaganda call all Serbs Chetniks making no distinction?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Were the families of JNA officers mistreated and harassed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: In this way were JNA officers blackmailed and made to surrender?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Were there cases when a JNA barracks was surrounded, the officers refused to surrender, the Croatian police and paramilitary forces brought members of their immediate families there and threatened that their families would be killed unless they surrendered?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do remember when Goran Hadzic was arrested at Plitvice in the first few days of April 1991?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Are you aware -- are you aware that the Serb Radical Party, in the course of March and April 1991, at the invitation of local Serbs sent their volunteers to many villages to participate in defending the population which felt under threat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: That was in March and April 1991; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: At the time the JNA did not participate in the armed clashes at all; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it didn't participate, but on the 2nd of March they arrived in Pakrac, and later on, on the 1st of April, it arrived in Plitvice.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I'll ask you about that separately. Now I want to maintain the continuity of this set of questions. You were one of the negotiators with the Croatian authorities negotiating the release of Goran Hadzic and his associates; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Goran Hadzic when he was arrested was beaten up, put in the boot of a police car; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And you as a negotiator with the Croatian authorities, did you manage to reach an agreement that the Croatian authorities should release Goran Hadzic and the Serbs should remove the barricades at the approaches to the villages in Eastern Slavonia and --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter is not sure where.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And the Croatian police would not intervene?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what we agreed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Are you aware whether these barricades were really dismantled?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were dismantled.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Are you aware that most volunteers of the Serb Radical Party then withdrew to Serbia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that small groups in individual villages remained even after the signing of that agreement and that one such group remained in Borovo Selo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that the Croats with two busloads of policemen, both regular policemen and extra -- irregular policemen and the speedily mobilised policemen, burst into Borovo Selo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Are you aware that they began to shoot as soon as they disembarked from the buses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Are you aware that the first person killed in Borovo Selo was a Serb, Vojislav Milic, a volunteer from a village near Valjevo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you hear that he was killed although he was not carrying a weapon? He was killed in front of the cultural club where a group of volunteers was quartered?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Are you aware that volunteers of the Serb Radical Party started fighting only then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Are you aware that the local people were working in the fields at the time because it was time to sow corn and other agriculture crops?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And that it took some time for them to hear the shooting, collect their weapons and start fighting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Are you aware that large number of Croatian policemen and para-policemen were killed in that fighting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Are you aware that the fighting stopped only when a JNA unit entered Borovo Selo and separated the warring sides?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Are you aware that the Croatian authorities demanded that the JNA unit intervene?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: It was only then that the Croats managed to pull out of Borovo Selo, collect the wounded and the dead; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. They did that with the assistance of the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So practically the JNA took the Croats' side at that time and helped them not to suffer an even greater defeat.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the JNA then separated the two sides and allowed the wounded and the dead to be pulled out.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Had there not been the JNA intervention, it would have been hard for any Croatian policeman to pull out alive; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, most probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Are you aware that at that time the Croatian authorities had already mobilised foreigners into their paramilitary units?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about that later.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you hear that many Kurd mercenaries were in their units?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, a lot of things were being said at the time, that people of different nationalities were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you hear that the Croats took these poor, illiterate, and rather primitive Kurds and that they paid them in false money with banknotes that had long not been valid, the banknotes used in Pavelic's Independent State of Croatia and even Hitler's Reich marks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't hear that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you hear that the Croats did not count Kurds who had been killed among their losses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard something about that but I don't really know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you hear that these Kurds were simply buried somewhere as if they had never even turned up in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't hear that. I didn't hear about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Very well. You saw this footage shown to you by the OTP where I'm declaring Stipe Mesic to be a Ustasha. You remember that, don't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Are you aware that Stipe Mesic was one of Franjo Tudjman's closest associates?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Are you aware that at the time of the election campaign in Croatia when the elections were being prepared Stipe Mesic visited the Ustasha emigres in overseas countries?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Are you aware that there is video footage showing Stipe Mesic singing Ustasha songs at rallies where Pavelic's pictures were displayed and Ustasha iconography?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw footage where Mr. Stipe Mesic spoke about the double victory of Croatia on the 10th of April when the Ustasha came to power and again in 1945 when the partisans won. He spoke of two victories, the victory of the Ustasha government and the victory of the partisan government.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: It's the 10th of April, 1941, when under German occupation the Ustasha took over power in Croatia and declared the independent State of Croatia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: That was the 10th of April. The Croats won both when the Ustasha gained power and after World War II when the partisans gained power. Both times they were among the victors. Is that the gist of Stipe Mesic's words?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's how he spoke to the rally in Australia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, I'll he deal with these rallies very briefly; it would take too long to deal with each of them in detail. In the summer and autumn of 1991, did it sometimes happen that in Sisak Serbs would simply go missing? Sisak is a town close to Western Slavonia and close to Banija; is that correct? Banija is the closest to it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Sisak is in Banija and these things did happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: It would simply happen that a Serb would go missing, would be swallowed up by the night and no one would know about their fate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did some of -- were some of these Serbs later found in the river Sava?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Were Serbs killed there in their houses and armed groups would simply turn up and kill them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: In Sisak, were there any armed conflicts?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the town itself, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So Croatian paramilitary units killed Serb civilians even though there was no conflict going on, no fighting. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know about the Croatian camps in Pakracka Poljana, and Marino Selo close to Pakrac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I heard about them. I know about them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Were Serb civilians brought there from various places in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Were there Serb civilians from Zagreb among them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Were many of these Serbs killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did many of these Serbs have to pay vast sums of money to get out of those camps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So one of the motives of putting the Serbs into camps was to extort money from them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Slavonska Pozega is close to Western Slavonia, is it not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that the Crisis Staff of the defence of the municipality of Slavonska Pozega ordered in writing that all Serbs be evacuated from 25 villages in a 48-hour period with the belongings they could carry with them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Was that on the 29th of October, 1991?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Were these villages in which there had been no fighting, no armed conflicts?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Those Serbs who were not evacuated, were they killed in their houses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And all the houses in those villages, were they looted and burnt?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Was this the big -- the first big example of ethnic cleansing in the wars that were conducted in the territory of the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you remember the events at the Korana bridge on the 21st of September, 1991?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did a group of JNA soldiers then run into an ambush set by Croatian paramilitary units?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And when asked to surrender, did these JNA soldiers really surrender?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: When they surrendered, did they lay down their arms, and were they then made to lie down on the bridge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And was fire opened on them, and were they slaughtered with knives?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Under public pressure much later was there an attempt to prosecute the perpetrators of this crime?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The trial is still ongoing.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, the trial is still ongoing. Evidently there's procrastination. It's being delayed.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: On the 1st of November was there a general attack on the civilians in Grubisno Polje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Is Grubisno Polje to the north-west of Pakrac, and there were no armed conflicts there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Grubisno Polje is to the north-west of Pakrac, but there was fighting there in August and September 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But it was sporadic fighting. There were no serious battles.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there were no serious battles.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: One could say that there was -- there was skirmishes. Is that the right expression?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wasn't there but there was shooting.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: As early as the 15th of October did an exodus of civilians begin from the area of Grubisno Polje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was the first exodus of Serbs in Western Slavonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Was the exodus caused by the news that the Croats were preparing for a major attack on Grubisno Polje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: When the Croats burst into Grubisno Polje there weren't many civilians left there; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And those who did remain were killed in spite of this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some of those who remained were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: A number of civilians took refuge in the woods near Grubisno Polje; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did the Croats burn down that wood in order to kill the Serbs who were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, people spoke about this, but it was not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, most of the Serbs managed to escape that wood, but those who remained were burnt?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think they were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: They were killed and then they were burnt?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Mr. 004, do you remember the events in Zagreb in December 1991, when the police killed an entire family, the Zec family?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Zec family was killed but two children survived, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: A mother -- a mother, a father, and a 12-year-old daughter were taken to Mount Sljeme near Zagreb; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: The mother and the father were killed immediately?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: The 12-year-old daughter was first raped and then killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did it turn out that the perpetrators of that crime were people from Franjo Tudjman's personal security guards?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: After a long time, after many years, were these perpetrators put on trial?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there was a trial, but they did not have a lawyer when they were interviewed, and they could not be tried.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So they were released for procedural reasons, although the facts were established showing that they had perpetrated the crime?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-004 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We will stop now because it's time to stop and to adjourn. We will start tomorrow at 8.30. I would like to tell Mr. Seselj that you will have three hours and eight minutes left for the cross-examination. So we will meet again tomorrow at 8.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 13th day of February, 2008, at 8.30 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.15 p.m.,
